root_cause: The JS API (26) job's 'E2E of openvino-node package' step failed on a Windows runner. The PR (#37225) only modifies NPU plugin test files and has no changes to the JS/Node.js codebase. This is consistent with a well-documented recurring flaky pattern in the OpenVINO CI for JS API E2E tests on Windows, particularly around Electron binary cleanup/permission errors on AKS Windows runners. The step completed in under 2 minutes, suggesting a transient startup or cleanup failure rather than a logic error. Job logs were not accessible via the MCP tooling (secrecy policy), so the exact error line could not be confirmed.
reproduction_steps: N/A - transient Windows runner issue unrelated to PR changes
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed job - the failure appears transient and unrelated to the NPU test changes
If failures continue on Node 26 JS API E2E, investigate whether the Node 26 runner image has Electron permission issues similar to the known pattern (85df26485ff568d8)
prevention_strategies: The recurring JS API E2E flakiness on Windows should be addressed at the infrastructure level (e.g., runner cleanup hooks, or excluding Electron binary from reuse across test runs).
historical_context: Pattern 85df26485ff568d8 'JS API E2E Electron cleanup fails on Windows - Permission denied removing locked electron.exe/dll' has 16 occurrences; pattern 323dd65ac8d70bf1 'JS API E2E of openvino-node package fails on Windows' occurred once on 2026-08-06. The PR itself (NPU test ports) is completely unrelated to JS API.
